What was unexpressible before this stage was the TANGLER effect's runtime consequence, and it is measured: docs/findings/2026-10-28-t452-r02-ordnance-effects-fuses-and-swarm.md section 1 measured that a TANGLER record installs a tick callback (0x4ba877), that the fire path builds the field object at 0x4b94e0 with the record's RADIUS (image default 10.0 m at 0x4ba870; no retail wep_ record states RADIUS) and TIME (weP_12 2 s), that its tick 0x4b9590 subtracts the frame time and, while positive, walks the actor list and calls the weapon's per-hit routine for every actor whose squared distance is below RADIUS squared, the owner included, and removes the field at zero; docs/findings/2026-10-28-t452-tangler-effect.md measured what that hit does: the per-hit routine's TANGLER branch (0x4b9ded) zeroes both damage channels and applies a tangle of duration max(2.0 s, 10.0 * (1 - exposure / RADIUS)) with the constants at 0x6032dc/0x62b124/0x62b120, that a re-hit raises the timer at +0x2e0 and never shortens it, that three actor updates count it down and clear the flag, that the force routine 0x48fc40 stores 0.0 into its local force scalar [ebp-8] while the flag is set, and that the boost setter 0x4b2110 refuses to enable while the flag is set (a tangle ends a boost). The runtime expression this report records: the field opens at fire time from the launch order's own pose (the same pose the launch effect reports), lives TIME in whole 30 Hz ticks, re-applies the tangle to every actor inside RADIUS squared each tick, the owner included, and exposes a timed tangled state whose remaining ticks a flight consumer reads; a launch of a component with no registered field opens none.
